transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 11:00 AM PST / 19:00 CET
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CISO, PulseMed), Tom Brennan (Head of Platform, PulseMed), Priya Shah (Legal, PulseMed)

Summary: Brief security review focused on data residency and region pinning requirements for PulseMed's EU patient data flows. Covered SOC 2/ISO status, how Redwood routes requests and pins regions, encryption/KMS options, audit log retention, and sub-processor disclosures. Agreed next steps to share artifacts and schedule legal follow-up.

Transcript: 
00:00 Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm ava with redwood inference, with me is marco, our solutions engineer. how are you all?
00:12 Dr. Lena: hey thanks, good morning, yes joining from berlin, a few of us here.
00:18 Tom: morning, quick background, we're picking a partner for model inference for our clinical notes pipeline, key must is that we keep EU patient data in EU, euro data residency.
00:30 Marco: sure, thanks tom. quick follow, when you say keep in EU do you mean region pinning for both inference and logs, or just generated outputs?
00:44 Tom: inference and logs, and we need to avoid any cross-border processing unless we have teraprovide a legal basis.
00:53 Ava: got it. we'll run through how our hosted and private options handle region pinning. note that we have hosted eu regions, dedicated pools, and private vpc deployments — each has different tradeoffs.
01:06 Dr. Lena: also SOC 2 and iso, do you have reports? and do you support SSO with SAML + SCIM for provisioning?
01:17 Ava: yes, we are SOC 2 Type 2 and have ISO 27001 attestation. i'll share the report, it's in our security folder. we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning and role based access control.
01:31 Priya: for legal we need details on sub-processors and whether any tokenization or key material leaves EU. what about kms?
01:40 Marco: good question. by default our hosted offering uses regional key management per cloud provider; for EU residents we can encrypt using EU KMS and we also offer customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-kms for Dedicated and Private deployments.
01:56 Tom: can you confirm that model inference compute and kv cache never go to US for EU pinned requests?
02:04 Marco: so with region pinning on the hosted product we route requests to the EU cluster, and runtime fetches model shards from the EU cache where available. caveat: in some legacy cases model shards may be in s3 cross-region for efficient loading, but we have a guaranteed path for EU-locked deployments — we can discuss pre-warming models in EU storage to avoid cross-border pulls.
02:28 Dr. Lena: when you say guaranteed, is that contractual? we need it in dpa.
02:33 Ava: that's doable. we have DPA clauses for region-pinning obligations and sub-processor lists; we'll send the template.
02:40 Tom: about audit logs — how granular and what's the retention? we need 7 years for some records.
02:47 Marco: we capture token-level request/response headers, routing metadata, and admin actions in audit logs. retention is configurable: hosted default is 90 days, enterprise can extend to multi-year with retention add-on. logs for EU pinned data can be stored in eu-only storage.
03:05 Priya: are logs pseudonymized? any pii in logs?
03:10 Marco: we redact sensitive payloads by default and provide options to exclude full payloads from logs; but note that application-level pseudonymization is recommended before sending PHI.
03:22 Ava: for highly regulated customers we usually recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with KMS and VPC to meet strict residency and audit controls.
03:31 Dr. Lena: our preference is hosted EU but with contractual guarantees and keys in EU. we want to avoid private unless cost-prohibitive.
03:40 Marco: reasonable. for hosted EU we can enable region pinning + customer-managed KMS so keys never leave EU. that satisfies encryption-at-rest with EU KMS. for in-transit we use TLS with strong ciphers.
03:53 Tom: how do you handle sub-processors; do you have a list and do they have access to plaintext?
04:01 Ava: we maintain a sub-processor list; none have access to plaintext for encrypted customer payloads when customer-managed keys are used. otherwise some operational subs may have limited access under NDAs. we'll share the current list and the date of last update.
04:17 Priya: can we get SOC 2 bridge letter and evidence of penetration tests?
04:23 Ava: yes, SOC 2 Type 2 report plus yearly pentest summary — sharing after NDA where required.
04:31 Tom: there may be cross-border law enforcement requests, does redwood notify customers for subpoenas?
04:38 Marco: we follow a notification policy unless prohibited by law; in many cases we notify customers and provide the legal process contacts.
04:47 Dr. Lena: ok good. one more technical: when a request is routed to EU cluster, is session affinity guaranteed for KV cache hits across subsequent calls?
04:59 Marco: we provide session affinity within the region; cache is per-region. if you use multi-region failover, you may see misses but we can configure sticky routing for a given tenant to prefer a single EU cluster.
05:15 Speaker 1: sorry quick interruption, how about latency impact if we force eu-only vs using us fallback?
05:22 Marco: forcing eu-only increases tail latency for models that have most infra in us, but for our EU-optimized models or pre-warmed eu pools latency is comparable. dedicated capacity gives the best tail latencies.
05:38 Tom: pricing delta for dedicated vs hosted?
05:41 Ava: we'll follow up with pricing, generally dedicated has committed capacity and fixed monthly fees; hosted is usage-based. we'll send a pricing sheet.
05:50 Priya: on contract language, we need region pinning in DPA plus indemnity for improper transfers. can you support that?
05:58 Ava: we can review redlines; our legal team supports region-specific DPA clauses, we'll prep a suggested clause.
06:06 Dr. Lena: any EU data residency certifications or local attestations?
06:12 Marco: we have EU data centers compliant with local laws; ISO 27001 applies to those environments. we can share the attestation.
06:20 Tom: ok let's recap next steps and artifacts to share.
06:25 Ava: sure — i'll send SOC 2 report, iso summary, current sub-processor list, and a DPA template. marco will send a region-pinning architecture doc and KMS integration notes.
06:36 Priya: we'll review and send back questions and redlines.
06:40 Ava: great, can we aim to have the docs over by monday dec 7th?
06:46 Dr. Lena: yes that works for us.
06:49 Ava: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up on schedule for legal call wk of dec 14.
06:55 Tom: thanks all.

End of transcript.
